title: Codified Context: Infrastructure for AI Agents in a Complex Codebase
fallos_mitigaciones: Symptom-cause-fix tables per subsystem prevent recurring bugs (e.g. DNS-desync scar, save-tier corruption); knowledge-gap detection when MCP retrieval returns zero results (case study 3, drop-system) surfaces undocumented subsystems before risky refactors.
cita: Vasilopoulos, A. (2026). Codified Context: Infrastructure for AI Agents in a Complex Codebase.
notes: Systems/experience-report, no controlled ablation -> CUALITATIVA (Sec 4.1). Sec 3 tiered arch: T1 constitution ~660L hot-load / T2 19 specialist agents ~9300L / T3 34 KB docs ~16250L, MCP retrieval uses keyword substring matching (Sec 3.3.1) -> retrieval=GREP-ARCHIVOS. Sec 4.2-4.3 quant: 283 sessions, 2801 human prompts, 16522 agent turns, 1478 MCP calls/218 sessions (usage counts, not precision -> mide_lectura=NO). 4 case studies Sec 4.4 (save-system 74 sessions zero bugs; UI-sync pattern reuse; drop-system knowledge-gap-as-signal; RNG determinism collaborative debugging). multiagente=SI: 19 domain-expert agents share T1/T3 knowledge via orchestration trigger table. trigger=DISCRECIONAL-LLM: specs 'generated and updated by the AI at the developer's direction', no deterministic write rule defined.

title: Shared Selective Persistent Memory for Agentic LLM Systems
benchmarks: Superstore Sales; UCI Adult Income; NYC 311 Service Requests; World Bank GDP
fallos_mitigaciones: Full-history persistence causes 'trace anchoring': agent biased toward stale prior solution paths, degrading completion 8pp below no-memory baseline (Sec 6.2/7, Table 1-2); mitigated by selective forgetting (Sec 3.3): discard reasoning traces, tool-invocation logs, error-recovery paths, raw data; keep only 4 structured memory categories.
cita: Pedada, S., Dhavala, A., & Patil, N. (2026). Shared Selective Persistent Memory for Agentic LLM Systems.
notes: Sec 3.2 decomposes memory into Mtask/Mdata/Mtools/Moutput, persisted to MongoDB + git-versioned artifacts (Eq.1-3) -> representacion=HIBRIDA. Sec 3.3 explicit 'selective forgetting' (deterministic app-layer filtering at session end, not LLM judgment) -> trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA; retrieval=NA (no ranking/search step, all 4 categories composed wholesale into next prompt, Eq.1-2). Table 1 ablation (no-mem 79% / full-hist 71% / selective 96% completion, 24 enterprise tasks); Table 2 public-dataset replication (12/12 zero-token refresh trials); Table 3 summary-driven token reduction 97-946x -> F add COSTO. Sec 3.5 zero-token refresh checks schema-compatibility before reuse (staleness/fidelity gate) -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI. F facet MULTIAGENTE kept from screening (workspace 'shared...collaborative' across users, Sec 1.1 UC2) though strict RQ4 multiagente=NO (collaboration is human-user sharing via RBAC, not multiple AI agents; single agentic engine per session, Sec 5). Moutput = runtime-injection 'contract' between artifact and data -> handoff includes CONTRATO. Use cases include explicit cross-team org sharing (Sec 1.1 UC2) -> alcance adds ORGANIZACION.

title: Enhancing SWE Bench with Context Engineering: A Comparative Study Against Prompt Engineering in LLM-Based Software Tasks
fallos_mitigaciones: Hallucination detection (AST-based validation flagging non-existent APIs, incorrect signatures, phantom dependencies) tracked as a metric (Sec 2.3, 'Comprehensive Metrics Collection'); no explicit mitigation strategy is described beyond flagging results.
cita: Murugesan, T. (2026). Enhancing SWE Bench with Context Engineering: A Comparative Study Against Prompt Engineering in LLM-Based Software Tasks.
notes: RECONSIDERAR: paper reads as likely synthetic/low-substance (single-author, generic citations to unnamed venues [1]-[4] for all quantitative claims, illustrative Python code blocks in Sec 2.3 contain syntax gaps typical of AI-generated pseudocode) -- decision left to human per protocol. mem_tipos=NA per rule 5: paper is NOT about persistent cross-session memory, it measures single-task 'context engineering' (repo history/docs/architecture injected per SWE-bench task, discarded after) vs prompt engineering on SWE-bench success (Sec 2.3 Methodology, 240 stratified tasks, 3 conditions: baseline/prompt-eng/context-eng). retrieval=RANKING: 3-stage pipeline (traversal, relevance scoring, structuring) explicitly scores/prioritizes context (Sec 2.2). mide_lectura=SI: hybrid scoring reports '78% alignment with expert developer judgments of context relevance' (Sec 2.3) -> F requires+gets RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (differs from F_screening=DOCS-VERSIONADO only). Sec 2.4: context-eng +29.3% avg success on complex multi-component tasks vs +4.2% for prompt-eng alone; prompt-eng +14% on simple single-file tasks. F also adds COSTO (extensive token/resource-consumption metrics, Sec 2.3).

title: .ava: A Compressed Symbolic Notation for Persistent AI Agent Memory
fallos_mitigaciones: V3 dataset design (overweighted key symbols x15, 5 epochs) caused severe overfitting, worse than V2 on nearly all metrics (Sec 4.3.3, 'echec'); mitigated in V4/V4b by switching to prompt/completion loss (SFTTrainer), zero duplication with paraphrase diversity, and tuning to 3 epochs (Sec 4.3.4-4.3.5).
cita: Cros, A. & Ava (2026). .ava -- Une notation symbolique compressee pour la memoire persistante d'agents IA.
notes: Sec 2.5 Table 2: measured compression on real MEMORY.md (~24K char -> ~800 char, ~30x, full file 661 lines). Sec 4.3.5 V4b fine-tune result: loss 0.999, token accuracy 78.5% (vs 51% for V4 1-epoch) on Qwen2.5-1.5B/6GB VRAM LoRA -> evidencia_tipo=ABLATION (V1-V4b dataset/training iterations, Table with loss/accuracy per phase) + MEDICION-COSTO (compression ratios Table 2, GPU/time Sec 4.3.5). Sec 3.5: 4-layer memory hierarchy L1 active-context / L2 hot .ava (WRITE) / L3 warm semantic-search via Ollama+nomic-embed-text (retrieval=EMBEDDINGS) / L4 cold full archive never deleted (explicit anti-OLVIDO design principle, Sec 3.4: 'IA doit garder tout'). Sec 2.3 vocabulary includes project-state symbols (triangle=project name/stack/metrics, with terminal state active/paused/off/dead/merged) -> plan_estado=SI (project/progress state IS memory content). F_screening=DOCS-VERSIONADO confirmed (.ava files are git-versionable plain text, Sec 2.2 principle 4); F adds COSTO since compression/token-economy is the paper's central contribution.

title: SWE-Adept: An LLM-Based Agentic Framework for Deep Codebase Analysis and Structured Issue Resolution
fallos_mitigaciones: Failed-hypothesis reversion via checkpoint rollback: agent reverts to prior semantic-step checkpoint when later edits fail, then branches a new hypothesis (Sec 3.3, Fig 2 a-2); Table 4 ablation shows resolve-rate drop when substituting SWE-Adept's designed planning/checkpointing module with SWE-agent's free-form think-and-edit loop.
cita: He, K., & Roy, K. (2026). SWE-Adept: An LLM-Based Agentic Framework for Deep Codebase Analysis and Structured Issue Resolution.
notes: Sec 3.1 code-structure tree (tree-sitter, dependency graph) drives agent-directed depth-first search (Fig 1) -> retrieval=GRAFO; Table 1 reports Acc@3(file)/Acc@5(function) localization accuracy -> mide_lectura=SI, requires+has RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F (confirms F_screening). Sec 3.3 'backend working memory' (TRABAJO) stores hypothesis/todo/checkpoint metadata (git hash) keyed by semantic execution step -> representacion=HIBRIDA (structured metadata + git); trigger=CHECKPOINT (agent commits state 'after each completed to-do step', literal vocab match). Sec 3.3/Fig 2c: 'compile a comparative report across hypotheses... to support final selection' -> operaciones includes CONSOLIDACION. Table 2 resolve rate +2.8-4.3pp vs baselines on SWE-Bench Lite/Pro with GPT-5.2/Claude-4.5; Table 4-5 module + context-management ablations. hypothesis_plan todo lists w/ status [-]/[v]/[!] tracked in memory -> plan_estado=SI. handoff=PUNTEROS: resolution agent receives identified code locations (file+line 'anchors') from localization agent, not full content (Sec 3.3). Two-agent framework (localization+resolution) with separate context windows -> multiagente=SI, added to F (differs from F_screening which lacked MULTIAGENTE).

title: DocAware: Documentation-Augmented AI Agents for Reliable Code Review and API Migration
benchmarks: openai-v3; express-v4; stripe-v2; mongoose-v6; axios-v0 (self-constructed fixtures, Sec 4.2)
fallos_mitigaciones: Hallucination (findings referencing API names absent from retrieved docs) measured at 22.9-25.7% even WITH documentation (Sec 5.3, Table 2); mitigated but not eliminated via structured/version-specific doc retrieval + tool-use structured output; authors flag the metric only checks syntactic grounding, not semantic correctness (Sec 5.3/6.2).
cita: Chandrashekar, P. (2026). DocAware: Documentation-Augmented AI Agents for Reliable Code Review and API Migration.
notes: Sec 3.4 persistent memory layer: entry types review_finding/migration_decision/pattern/annotation, vector embeddings (all-MiniLM-L6-v2, 384-dim) + cosine-similarity JSON index -> representacion=VECTOR, retrieval=EMBEDDINGS. Sec 5.1 Table 2: 4-condition A/B/C/D ablation (F1 70.9%->86.8%, recall 76.4%->98.6%; D vs C isolates memory's contribution: +0.3 F1pp/+0.4 precisionpp) -> mide_lectura=SI (memory-read utility explicitly measured), F confirms RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO from F_screening. Sec 5.3: hallucination-rate is a central measured outcome across doc conditions -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI (paper's core claim is grounding/fidelity against version-specific docs). Sec 4.2: 5 self-built JS-library migration fixtures, 31 real issues + 6 decoys, not an established external benchmark. handoff=CONTENIDO: review findings/patterns/decisions persist and are retrieved in later review sessions of the same project (Sec 3.4, RQ4.Q3).

title: The Markdown Fallacy: Empirical Evidence That Format Is the Wrong Debate for LLM Memory Architecture
benchmarks: Custom 50-document/50-query Google-Ads-MCC benchmark (this paper, open-sourced); data.world KG benchmark and GraphRAG-Bench cited as external comparison points (Sec II-C)
fallos_mitigaciones: GraphRAG scored notably lower on Level-2 relational queries (0.731) because the extracted subgraph captured entities/relationships but lost the explanatory narrative/mechanism prose (Sec IV.D 'GraphRAG Level 2 Anomaly'); proposed direction is preserving explanatory metadata alongside structural relationships, not yet implemented.
cita: Williams, J. (2026). The Markdown Fallacy: Empirical Evidence That Format Is the Wrong Debate for LLM Memory Architecture.
notes: mem_tipos=NA per rule 5: this is a controlled measurement/benchmark study of FORMAT and RETRIEVAL-ARCHITECTURE effects on LLM reasoning accuracy, not a proposal of a persistent memory mechanism (Sec III Methodology, H1-H3). Stage 1 (Sec IV.A, N=900, Table I): markdown vs structured-relational encoding, format has no consistent directional effect (delta=-0.004 overall). Stage 2 (Sec IV.B, N=1200, Table II): full-context markdown (0.964) significantly beats Vector-RAG (0.888), GraphRAG (0.875) and Hybrid (0.904) on L3 strategic queries (ANOVA p<0.004) -> mide_lectura=SI (retrieval quality is THE measured variable), F confirms RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (matches F_screening). Table III: retrieval conditions retain only 10.6-16.2% of the 33,122-char corpus (84-90% information loss) -- reframes the debate as an information-budget/COSTO problem at production scale (Sec V.D 'Scale Threshold'), hence F adds COSTO.

title: Temporal-Stratified Retrieval for AI Agent Memory: A Structure-First Alternative to Vector Search
benchmarks: 500-atom / 100-query synthetic benchmark (self-constructed, reproducible via benchmarks/run_benchmark.py, Sec 4.1)
fallos_mitigaciones: Sec 5.2 Limitations: cannot match semantically-related-but-lexically-different queries without embeddings (e.g. 'revenue' vs 'sales'), only partially mitigated by explicit tagging; linear-scan manifest scoring degrades above ~10,000 atoms (no inverted index yet); scoring weights are hand-tuned/unvalidated on diverse domains.
cita: Hartmann, A. (2026). Temporal-Stratified Retrieval for AI Agent Memory: A Structure-First Alternative to Vector Search.
notes: Sec 3.1 atom schema: YAML frontmatter, 9 required fields, 14 types spanning episodic (incident/event/lesson/loss/win) and semantic (rule/insight/reference/concept) knowledge -> mem_tipos=EPISODICA;SEMANTICA. Sec 3.3 hot(<=2d)/warm(2-7d)/cold(>7d) temporal stratification by 'updated' field -> operaciones+CONSOLIDACION, trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA (time-threshold based, not LLM judgment). Sec 3.4 deterministic weighted keyword scoring (name/tag/project/description/path) + multi-keyword bonus + temporal bonus + archived(x0.3)/superseded(x0.5) status PENALTY -- the status penalty is an explicit staleness-aware scoring adjustment -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI; scoring=RANKING (not plain grep, it's a multi-factor weighted algorithm). Sec 4.1 benchmark (500 atoms/100 queries): mean latency 1.62ms, 100/100 top-1 precision on tag-matched queries, hot layer top-1 in 66% of cases -> mide_lectura=SI confirms RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (matches F_screening). Sec 4.2 production deployment (470 atoms/14 projects) explicitly labelled 'observational findings (not controlled measurements)' -> evidencia_tipo adds CUALITATIVA alongside the controlled BENCHMARK-E2E.

title: Beyond RAG: LLM Wikis as Living Semantic Memory: Patterns, Empirical Findings, and Open Problems
benchmarks: Self-constructed studies, no named external benchmark: CLS-Wiki consolidation-gating study (AUC), cross-institutional policy-retrieval citation-recall study, confidence-calibration (ECE) study, KTRR six-layer routing study on a 2,718-unit NingboTech AI-course corpus (111 files, academic years 2021-2026, Sec 3.1)
fallos_mitigaciones: Abstract/Sec4.2: 'the wiki pattern failed to outperform RAG in two tested domains' (explicit negative result). Sec 2.5: three degenerate-compiler failure modes (fragmentation, atomisation, over-merging) plus an 'LLM filter saturation' regime -- an ingest-value pre-filter becomes uninformative (assigns high value to nearly every document) when the wiki is small relative to the incoming document stream, characteristic of the early flywheel phase; no full fix proposed, flagged as a deployment risk.
cita: Zhang, B. (2026). Beyond RAG: LLM Wikis as Living Semantic Memory: Patterns, Empirical Findings, and Open Problems.
notes: Self-described 'position paper... not a system description' synthesising first-person empirical sub-studies -> evidencia_tipo mixes ABLATION/MEDICION-COSTO/CUALITATIVA. Sec 2.4: wiki-based retrieval citation recall 0.242+-0.21 vs BM25-RAG 0.095+-0.12 (2.5x) on cross-institutional policy queries -> mide_lectura=SI, F+RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO. Sec 2.2 CLS-Wiki study: outcome-surprise AUC=0.720 predicting episodic-to-semantic consolidation value. Sec 2.3: raw LLM-confidence-label Expected Calibration Error 0.528, reduced to 0.311 by post-hoc propagation framework. Sec 3.1 six-layer KTRR knowledge lattice (Raw/Wiki/Protocol/Metadata/Fact/Rule) with cost-sensitive LLM-judged ingest-routing classifier -> operaciones+ADMISION. Sec3.2-3.3 lint/contradiction-detection + staleness/drift + Sec3.4 provenance/audit-trails -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI (central contribution). 'Failed to outperform RAG in two tested domains' -> F NEGATIVO sense(b): evidence AGAINST the memory approach (per rule7), matches F_screening. Sec 7.2 distributed/multi-agent wikis explicitly named an OPEN problem, not implemented -> multiagente=NO.

title: CommitDistill: A Lightweight Knowledge-Centric Memory Layer for Software Repositories
benchmarks: 5 public repos (self-constructed illustrative case study, Sec V.B): psf/requests, pallets/flask, expressjs/express, redis/redis, junit-team/junit5 (25,000 commits); git log --grep and BM25 used as comparison baselines, not named external benchmarks
fallos_mitigaciones: RQ5 (n=200, two LLM judges): no retrieval condition (CommitDistill, BM25, or CD-Hybrid) produces a statistically detectable lift over a no-retrieval control on the headline mean, and CD-Hybrid is indistinguishable from BM25 head-to-head -- an explicit negative downstream-utility finding, honestly reported rather than hidden (Sec I / VI-G2). Mitigation for over-confident retrieval: calibrated silence threshold theta=2.5 gives a 'helps or stays silent' abstention property on out-of-corpus/OOD queries (Sec VI-E).
cita: Chukkapalli, D., Avula, T., Aggarwal, A., Singh, H., & Tallanki, A. (2026). CommitDistill: A Lightweight Knowledge-Centric Memory Layer for Software Repositories.
notes: Abstract: 1,167 typed units (Facts/Skills/Patterns) from 25,000 commits, useful-precision 0.525 @ Cohen's kappa=0.633 (40 dual-annotated Python units, RQ2) -> mem_tipos=SEMANTICA(Facts);PROCEDIMENTAL(Skills);EPISODICA(Patterns, recurring past-failure records). Sec VI.D 'decisive empirical finding': budget-constrained hit-rate at 256-char/query CommitDistill 0.750 vs BM25 0.333 vs git-log-grep 0.083 -> mide_lectura=SI (F+RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, matches F_screening). Sec III.D: extraction triggers as a post-merge/post-issue git hook -> EVENTO-DETERMINISTA. Sec II.C.3/IV.D: every unit carries commit-SHA/author/date provenance, stored as plain diffable JSON, reviewable via git diff -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI ('trust-instrumented memory substrate'). RQ5 top-3 typed units prepended to an LLM coding assistant's context at decision time (Sec V.A) -> handoff=CONTENIDO. Authors explicitly frame the evaluation as an 'illustrative case study... not for hypothesis testing' (Sec V.A) and report the null RQ5 result forthrightly -> F NEGATIVO sense(b), matches F_screening.

title: Skill-as-Pseudocode: Refactoring Skill Libraries to Pseudocode for LLM Agents
fallos_mitigaciones: Motivating failure mode (Sec 1): a 'confused -> re-retrieve -> still confused' loop where prose skill docs force the agent to re-derive schema+invocation syntax on every retrieval, producing off-by-one action errors ('put X in/on Y' vs 'move X to Y'); mitigated by the typed-contract + concrete-action-template dual signal (Sec 3.5, Fig 2). 2/10 SkillsBench SaP runs still crashed mid-execution (court-form-filling, data-to-d3) despite token savings (Sec 5.3).
cita: Li, X., Zang, Y., Cao, Y., & Sun, A. (2026). Skill-as-Pseudocode: Refactoring Skill Libraries to Pseudocode for LLM Agents.
notes: Sec3.3 four-check deterministic verifier (Coverage, Binding, Replacement, Risk) gates which candidate clusters get promoted into typed contracts kappa (trigger/input_schema/output_schema/pre-postconditions) -> operaciones ADMISION; Coverage+Replacement checks explicitly verify the compiled contract stays faithful to / coherently substitutes the source prose -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI. Table1: ALFWorld 134-game pooled 3 seeds (n=402): SaP wins 82 vs GoS 47 (+74% relative, pooled McNemar p=8.2e-5) at -22.8+-6.4% input tok / -17.3+-5.1% output tok / -14.5+-4.1% LLM calls per game -> mide_lectura=SI (the paper's central claim IS that the retrieved-content REPRESENTATION improves downstream task success), F+RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (differs from F_screening, noted here). Table3: pipeline ablation (deterministic-only -> +RC -> +BE) each stage adds ~5pp reward, ALFWorld 20-game pilot. Table2: SkillsBench 10-task (gpt-5-codex): SaP 3/10 vs GoS 2/10 at -43% input tokens. Sec3.1: cross-parent factoring promotes contracts callable in multiple parent skills to shared child skills -> operaciones CONSOLIDACION. Retrieval-time 'substituted bundle' (Fig2) delivers concrete action templates + rewritten parent skeleton + inlined typed contract -> handoff=CONTENIDO;CONTRATO (kappa literally named a 'contract' with trigger/I-O schema/pre-post-conditions).

title: Bridging Requirements and Architecture: Multi-Agent Orchestration with External Knowledge and Hierarchical Memory
benchmarks: 10-case SRS dataset (self-constructed, Table 2); baseline comparison against MetaGPT (not a named external benchmark)
fallos_mitigaciones: RQ2 (Sec 5.2/Table 4): RAG-based knowledge infusion improves component coupling/abstraction and mitigates 'God Object' anti-patterns seen in the noRAG condition, but REDUCES cohesion and increases interface/behavioral-state complexity inconsistently across the 10 projects -- 'does not consistently improve all quality metrics', a mixed/negative finding about the memory-infusion mechanism reported forthrightly.
cita: Li, R., Zhang, Y., Zhou, X., Cai, Y., Liang, P., Sun, W., Xuan, J., Jin, Z., & Liu, Y. (2026). Bridging Requirements and Architecture: Multi-Agent Orchestration with External Knowledge and Hierarchical Memory.
notes: Sec3.1/3.3, Fig1: explicit 3-tier hierarchical memory (per-agent working memory + per-agent episodic memory recording design experiences + framework-level SHARED semantic memory distilled from software projects/literature/expert knowledge, citing cognitive-architecture ref [49]) -> mem_tipos=TRABAJO;EPISODICA;SEMANTICA (literal vocab match). 4 specialized agents (Analyst/Modeler/Designer/Evaluator) ALL access the shared semantic memory (Sec3.1: 'all agents can access and retrieve') -> multiagente=SI, added to F (differs materially from F_screening=DOCS-VERSIONADO only, flagged). RQ2/Table4: RAG(with) vs noRAG structural+quantitative ablation across 10 SRS cases isolates the knowledge-infusion effect -> mide_lectura=SI, F+RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (also differs from screening). Evaluator agent produces an ATAM evaluation report + a 'mismatch analysis report' explicitly checking consistency between generated artifacts and requirements at every pipeline stage -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI, F+FIDELIDAD. Shared semantic memory 'distills' knowledge from prior sources -> operaciones+CONSOLIDACION. F_screening's DOCS-VERSIONADO is a comparatively WEAK fit (paper's 'documentation' = produced architecture-doc OUTPUT artifact, not a git-versioned memory-file substrate like the other papers in this batch); kept for the reviewer's spot-check per rule4.
